hasbro_patent_size_hardness.quote: the foam balls 12 may each have a diameter range of about 22.5 to about 23.5 mm; a hardness of about 1.5 to 2.1 Kg or less than 55 Durometer Shore A
hasbro_patent_size_hardness.used_for: diameter spec band; the hardness bracket for the foam stiffness sweep (the deflection at 1.5-2.1 kgf is not stated)

blasterhub_mass_fps.quote: Rival rounds only averaged 1.83g each ... Adventure Force 1.88g each, with little variation; 100 shots each: Rival 97 fps, AF 95 fps, none below 92 or above 101
blasterhub_mass_fps.used_for: Hasbro and Adventure Force mean mass; the 92-101 fps spread of a stock blaster (a launcher + ball spread we compare against)

worker_cheetah.quote: Dimensions: 22.7mm OD; Weight: 1.75g each; Material: EVA Foam; ultra-squishy EVA foam won't stall or burn out flywheels

dart_zone_powerstrike.quote: Featuring a 22.8mm diameter; Weight: 1.85g each; made with medium-density polyurethane foam
dart_zone_powerstrike.used_for: Dart Zone / Adventure Force size, mass, material

eva_foam_modulus.quote: closed-cell EVA: E = 2.77 / 4.27 / 5.37 / 5.48 / 6.98 MPa at 80 / 95 / 106 / 124 / 180 kg/m^3; stress at 10 % strain 0.09-0.29 MPa; strain rate has little influence on the elastic modulus
eva_foam_modulus.used_for: the small-strain modulus of EVA foam vs density (a Rival ball is ~290 kg/m^3: above this data, so the Hertz-effective modulus is swept, not taken from here)

pu_foam_ball_cor.quote: for a dry [PU foam] ball, e^2 = 0.55 is nearly constant [at hand-drop speeds]; the coefficient of restitution shows a strong decrease ... in the high-velocity regime
pu_foam_ball_cor.used_for: restitution bracket: e = 0.74 at low speed, lower at launch and impact speeds

eva_sheet_datasheet.quote: closed-cell EVA, 35 kg/m^3: rebound resilience 60 +- 5 % (ISO 4662); water uptake <= 12 % (ISO 7214)
eva_sheet_datasheet.used_for: the resilience and water-uptake order of magnitude for EVA foam (sheet, far lighter than a ball)

eva_friction.quote: Neat EVA: coefficient of friction 1.18 +- 0.03 (dry, vs alumina ball)
eva_friction.used_for: the upper end of the ball-on-tyre friction sweep

hasbro_flywheel_patent.quote: approximately 30% slippage can be measured between conventional flywheels and dart projectiles; tyres Shore 30A-90A; the tire may be allowed to expand approximately 4 mm in diameter when spinning
hasbro_flywheel_patent.used_for: slip is real on stock wheels (the friction sweep reaches down to 0.6); a spinning elastomer tyre grows (sim/turret_launch3d.py models the TPU tyre's centrifugal growth)

tpu95_ultimaker.quote: TPU 95A printed: Young's modulus 67 +- 6 MPa (XY), 56 +- 3 (Z); 96 Shore A; 1.22 g/cm^3
tpu95_ultimaker.used_for: the stiff end of the tyre modulus (small-strain, D3039)

tpu95_bambu.quote: Bambu TPU 95A HF: tensile modulus 9.8 +- 0.7 MPa (XY), 7.4 +- 0.6 (Z), ISO 527
tpu95_bambu.used_for: the soft end of the tyre modulus; the tyre growth sweep uses 10-30 MPa (NinjaTek Cheetah 26 MPa, Polymaker PolyFlex 33.6 MPa sit between)

hyper_hopper_patent.quote: soft spherical, but tacky, projectiles ... tend to aggregate or bind in the hopper and on the projectile feed track (14.8 mm TPE Hyper rounds, Shore A 3-30, not Rival foam)
hyper_hopper_patent.used_for: why rigid-sphere feed physics must be confirmed on the bench with real balls (tack is not modelled)

wet_rounds_forum.quote: performance is adversely affected by dirt, debris and moisture so scavenged rounds perform significantly differently to their dry counter-parts
wet_rounds_forum.used_for: wet/dirty balls are a different population: the damp condition is an estimate until the bench weighs soaked balls

hasbro.note: diameter: the middle of the patent band 22.5-23.5 (hasbro_patent_size_hardness); no measured mean is published

worn.note: est: a few hundred shots: 0.3 mm smaller, 40 % softer, fuzzier (grippier); the bench measures it

damp.note: est: picked up off damp grass: +30 % mass, softer, slippery on the tyre (wet_rounds_forum, eva_sheet_datasheet water uptake)

bench_plan.how: 50 balls per brand (Hasbro, Worker, Dart Zone/AF): calipers in two axes, 0.01 g scale; 20 of them again after 300 shots and after 10 min on wet grass
bench_plan.gives: d and m means and SDs per brand (replaces SD_D_MM, SD_M_G), the worn and damp scale factors

bench_plan.how: ball between two flat plates on a kitchen scale with a height gauge: force at 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 mm total squeeze, 10 balls per brand, new and worn
bench_plan.gives: the Hertz-effective modulus E (fit F = K d^1.5 with the two-plate R_eff) and the plateau
bench_plan.feeds: RANGES[E_mpa]; also checks the patent's 1.5-2.1 kg hardness

bench_plan.how: drop 10 balls from 1 m and from 2 m onto a tile; phone video at 240 fps; bounce height -> e = sqrt(h1/h0). Then fire at 55 fps into a plate and read the rebound on the same video
bench_plan.gives: e at 4.4 and 6.3 m/s, and at 17 m/s
bench_plan.feeds: RANGES[e] (launch damping, barrel bounces, the knock-down impulse)

bench_plan.test: Friction on the tyre and the barrel
bench_plan.how: a printed TPU 95A tile and a PETG tile on a tilting board; a ball under a 20 g and a 100 g weight in a printed cup; the angle it starts to slide; dry, damp, fuzzed

the barrel's two IR gates 50 mm apart (cad/turret.py barrel()); 20 shots at each of 6, 7, 8, 9, 9.4 and 10.4 krpm set speeds (AM32 telemetry), per brand; then 20 shots at 100 % throttle on the nominal rail and on the rail +4 %
bench_plan.gives: fps vs rpm (the launch efficiency eta), the SD per set speed, and the measured hardware ceiling
bench_plan.feeds: launch.json/launch3d.json: the set speed for 55 fps, the ceiling check (must be <= 70 fps on every brand, every shot)

bench_plan.how: strobe or high-speed video of the tyre edge against a scale at 0, 5, 9.4 and 10.4 krpm; or a dial gauge on a stopped wheel vs the chrono shift
bench_plan.gives: the TPU tyre's radial growth at speed

bench_plan.test: High-speed video of the nip and the muzzle
bench_plan.how: 1000+ fps phone video (or a Chronos) through a window in the cage: contact time, the ball's crush, slip (mark the ball), spin at the muzzle (mark the ball), exit angle vs the bore
bench_plan.gives: contact time (model: ~4.8 ms), spin, exit angle

bench_plan.how: paper targets at 2, 4, 6, 8 m, 20 shots each at the 55 fps set speed from a clamped turret; mark the laser dot; measure the group centre (drop, drift) and the 1-sigma radius
bench_plan.gives: drop vs range (drag Cd), drift (spin/Magnus), the dispersion budget
bench_plan.feeds: turret_flight validation (Cd, C_L), the accuracy check at 2/4/6 m

bench_plan.how: 300 balls through the feed at each pose (tilt 0 and -25, the robot leaned +-10 deg pitch, +-15 deg roll on a tilting bench), at 3/s and at the maximum rate; count misses, doubles, stalls (the feed servo's load reading), reverses; repeat with worn and damp balls and with the 30-ball and 5-ball hopper
bench_plan.gives: the feed reliability per pose and condition
bench_plan.feeds: feed.json / feed_dyn.json checks (model: 0 doubles, misses only by bridging)

bench_plan.how: the turret on the bench stand on a lazy-susan: pan at 90 deg/s with hard starts while feeding at 3/s; then drop the stand 20 mm onto a mat during a feed step
the printed game target (20 g plate, 4 deg rest lean) and a 150 g plywood plate at 2, 4, 6 m; 10 shots each; count knock-overs

not_published: within-brand size and mass spread (no SD, min/max or sample sizes anywhere reachable)
any force-deflection, durometer or bounce test of an actual Rival round
foam friction on TPU, rubber, PETG or nylon
mass of a soaked round; velocity vs shot count; temperature effects
